designSummary: Time-ordered measurement of a rare event with a chart of patient-days between injuries (g-chart) as the primary display and monthly rate charts as secondary.
sampleSize: The two wards have about 18,800 patient-days a year, so 41 injuries give a baseline of about 2.2 per 1,000 patient-days and a median of about 460 patient-days between injuries. Weekly counts would average fewer than one injury, so a weekly run chart would be mostly zeros. Over six months of cycles about 9,400 patient-days are expected; if the rate halves, about 10 injuries would occur instead of 20, and a g-chart would show a signal when two or more consecutive intervals exceed the upper limit or eight intervals lie above the baseline median. Six months is therefore the minimum period for a credible signal.
primaryAnalysis: g-chart of patient-days between successive category 2 or worse injuries, centre line and limits from the baseline year, with pre-specified rules: a single interval above the upper limit, or eight consecutive intervals above the baseline median. Limits are recalculated only after a sustained shift.
secondaryAnalysis: Monthly u-charts of injury rates split by nights worse or better than one nurse to seven; run charts of round completion, float availability, late night doses and patients woken.
missingData: Weeks without inspection are annotated and the patient-days are counted without assumed injuries; nights without a completion sheet are counted as not recorded, not as completed.
multiplicity: One primary chart carries the aim; other charts are descriptive and not tested.
software: Spreadsheet chart templates kept by tissue viability; limits checked by the hospital's quality analyst.
overfittingGuards: Chart type, counting rule and signal rules fixed before cycle 1
Baseline limits frozen until a sustained shift
Staffing split pre-specified; no other subgroups
Changes between cycles marked on the charts before new points are examined
summary: Rare events charted as patient-days between injuries; about six months of cycles needed for a credible signal.
